package_info.package_versions: all versions observed in campaign (e.g., @am-fe/hooks, @am-fe/provider, @am-fe/request, @am-fe/utils, @am-fe/watermark, @am-fe/watermark-core, @dynamic-form-components/mui, @dynamic-form-components/shineout, @expue/app, @fixedwidthtable/fixedwidthtable, @soc-fe/use, @spgy/eslint-plugin-spgy-fe, @virtualsearchtable/virtualsearchtable, shineouts)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain obfuscated or unobfuscated code that, upon installation, exfiltrates sensitive files such as SSH private keys, Kubernetes configuration, and system information to a remote attacker-controlled domain (app.threatest.com). The packages masquerade as legitimate libraries but include hidden data theft functionality, violating user trust and npm ecosystem norms.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, collects system information (username, hostname, public IP), and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in theft of sensitive credentials and host details.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses highly sensitive files (SSH private key and Kubernetes config) and system information immediately after package installation, then sends this data to an external, attacker-controlled domain. This behavior is not expected or justified for any legitimate npm package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not access or exfiltrate user SSH keys, Kubernetes configs, or system information during installation. Postinstall scripts are typically used for setup or dependency management, not for accessing or transmitting sensitive user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate enterprise deployment tool might collect system information for inventory or configuration purposes, but would never access or transmit private keys or configuration files to an untrusted third-party domain without explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config files during postinstall
Collection of username, hostname, and public IP address
Network exfiltration of collected data to app.threatest.com via HTTPS POST
Execution of code in the postinstall context, automatically triggered on install

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the obfuscated code reads sensitive files (such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config), collects system information (username, hostname, public IP), and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in covert credential and system data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to conceal the same malicious data theft and exfiltration behavior as in the unobfuscated variant, indicating deliberate intent to evade detection and hinder analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate postinstall scripts that access sensitive files and perform network exfiltration. Obfuscation in this context is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for protecting intellectual property in distributed libraries, but is not appropriate for scripts that run automatically and access user secrets during installation.
key_indicators: Obfuscated variable and function names in postinstall script
Same file and network access patterns as unobfuscated malicious code
References to app.threatest.com as exfiltration endpoint
Automatic execution in postinstall context with hidden data theft logic

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., fixedwidthtable or @am-fe/hooks).
Postinstall script executes, reading sensitive files (SSH keys, Kubernetes config) and collecting system information (username, hostname, public IP).
Collected data is exfiltrated via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials and system information.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts accessing ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config files
Collection of system information (username, hostname, public IP) during installation
Network requests to external domains (such as app.threatest.com) during postinstall execution
file_indicators: Presence of scripts/index.js containing code that accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
References to app.threatest.com in package scripts or code
Obfuscated JavaScript code in postinstall scripts (e.g., variable/function names like _0xabc)
network_indicators: Connections to Cloudflare IPs 172.67.141.49 and 104.21.9.30 during or immediately after npm install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.kube/config, or collect system information such as username, hostname, and public IP. Flag any package that sends data to external domains (especially app.threatest.com) during installation. Use static analysis to detect obfuscated code in scripts/index.js or similar files, and correlate with network activity to known malicious domains or IPs. Automated detection systems should alert on the combination of sensitive file access, system info collection, and outbound network requests in postinstall scripts.
